# Operational Model

## Certificate Lifecycle

Default TTLs are 1 hour for X.509 SVIDs, 24 hours for CAs, and 5-15 minutes
recommended for JWT-SVIDs. Rotation triggers at approximately two-thirds of the TTL
(~40 minutes for a 1-hour X.509 SVID).

## Caching and Availability

SPIRE Agents cache X.509 SVIDs locally, allowing workloads to continue
operating during server outages for the remaining duration of the SVID TTL [10].

JWT-SVIDs cannot be cached by design and require active server connectivity for
issuance. A server outage blocks all new JWT-SVID requests [10].

## High Availability

HA deployments require a minimum of two SPIRE servers sharing a PostgreSQL or
MySQL datastore. Each server runs its own CA instance [10].

The SPIRE sizing table covers deployment configurations from 10 to 10,000
workloads across 10 to 5,000 agents [10].

## Observability

Prometheus telemetry exposes critical metrics for certificate rotation health,
attestation success and failure rates, cache hit ratios, and datastore
performance.

## Failure Modes

Server downtime blocks new node/workload attestation and all JWT-SVID issuance.
KeyManager failures can cause cascading CA expiration if replacement keys cannot
be generated. Agent restart race conditions have been documented where agents
fail to re-attest before cached SVIDs expire [25].

## Production Deployments at Scale

Uber operates SPIRE across 250,000+ nodes, 4,500 services, and 4 cloud
providers. An LRU cache contribution reduced server CPU consumption by 40% and
enabled 2.5x more workloads per host group. A trend gauge mechanism replaced
simple health checks to better detect degradation [6].

Indeed runs SPIRE in production with 3,000 pods in a nested topology, with over
1 year of production operation. They tune resource allocation with Vertical Pod
Autoscaler and use DaemonSet rolling updates for agent upgrades [9].

## Staffing and Timeline

At scale, SPIRE deployments require 1-3 dedicated engineers. Deployment
timelines range from 6 months for smaller environments to 24 months for complex
multi-cluster, multi-cloud setups [7].

## Gaps and Limitations

1. Certificate rotation issues have been documented in the SPIRE issue tracker,
   including bad certificates after CA rotation and bundle propagation failures
   during grace periods [25].
2. CPU spikes to 150-160% have been observed under load [25].
3. Agent memory leaks reaching 3.5GB have been reported [25].
4. Debugging SPIRE failures is difficult due to inconsistent logging across
   components [25].
